blocks.x: How Agentic AI & Hyperautomation lands in Capabilities — the constraints that shape the build, the gated delivery pattern, and the deltas we commit against your baseline.

In Energy & Utilities, agentic ai & hyperautomation turns knowledge work into orchestrated autonomy. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: agentic process automation, digital workforce & multi-agent orchestration, decision intelligence systems — delivered on Dataq Swarm and Dataq Nexus and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Trading and scheduling decisions at market speed
Intraday markets reprice in minutes; scheduling, bidding and imbalance decisions run on spreadsheets and experience, not decision hubs.
Forecasting under intermittency
Renewable supply and flexible demand make legacy forecasting blind; imbalance costs and curtailment climb while forecasts run on yesterday's methods.
OT estate exposed by convergence
IT/OT convergence, remote access growth and legacy SCADA estates create attack paths with physical consequences; CIP/NIS2 duties expand faster than programs mature.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: NERC CIP (North America) and REMIT / MiFID II. Energy market conduct and reporting obligations. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Programs run on the fixed rhythm below, chosen so progress is legible from week one. The first quarter of the rhythm is verification: weeks 1–2 measure the current metric with your team and lock it by signature. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with your control owner receiving evidence weekly. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and the measured delta against the signed baseline. Gates are binding: miss one and the program stops or redirects with a documented decision.
